source_text: III. et ita idem Galerius Maximus proconsul in aliam diem Cyprianum sibi reservari praecepit. et eo tempore beatus Cyprianus ductus ad principem et stratorem eiusdem officii Galeri Maximi proconsulis clarissimi viri secessit, et in hospitio eius cum eo in vico qui dicitur Saturni inter Veneream et Salutariam mansit. Illic universus populus fratrum convenit. et cum hoc sanctus Cyprianus comperisset, custodiri puellas praecepit, quoniam omnes in [160 — scan unclear] ante ianuam hospitii principis manserant. Et ita altera die octava decima kalendarum Octobrium mane multa turba convenit ad Sexti secundum praeceptum Galeri Maximi proconsulis. et ita idem Galerius Maximus proconsul eadem die Cyprianum sibi offerri praecepit in atrio Sauciolo sedenti. cumque oblatus fuisset, Galerius Maximus proconsul Cypriano episcopo dixit: Tu es Thascius Cyprianus? Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Ego sum. Galerius Maximus proconsul dixit: Tu papam te sacrilegae mentis hominibus praebuisti? Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Ego. Galerius Maximus proconsul dixit: Iusserunt te sacratissimi imperatores caeremoniari. Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Non facio. Galerius Maximus ait: Consule tibi. Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Fac quod tibi praeceptum est. in re tam iusta nulla est consultatio.
pass_a_gloss: Literal gist: the same proconsul Galerius Maximus ordered Cyprian to be kept for another day; meanwhile blessed Cyprian withdrew, led to the chief officer and the attendant of that staff, and stayed in his lodging with him in the street called Saturn between Venerea and Salutaria; there the whole people of the brethren assembled, and when holy Cyprian learned this he ordered the young women to be guarded, because all had remained through a lost passage before the door of the chief officer's lodging; then on the next day, the eighteenth before the Kalends of October, in the morning a great crowd assembled at Sextus according to the proconsul's order, and the same Galerius Maximus ordered Cyprian to be presented to him on that day as he sat in the hall called Sauciolus, and when he had been presented Galerius asked whether he was Thascius Cyprian and Cyprian answered that he was, asked whether he offered himself as father to men of sacrilegious mind and Cyprian answered that he did, said the most sacred emperors commanded him to perform the rites and Cyprian said he does not do it, said take counsel for yourself and Cyprian answered do what has been commanded you, for in so just a matter there is no deliberation.
pass_b_english: And so the same Galerius Maximus the proconsul ordered Cyprian to be reserved for himself for another day.

In the meantime the blessed Cyprian, led to the chief officer and to the attendant of the staff of the same Galerius Maximus the proconsul, a man of most distinguished rank, withdrew apart, and he remained with him in his lodging in the street called Saturn, between Venerea and Salutaria.

There the whole people of the brethren came together, and when the holy Cyprian learned of this, he ordered that the young women be guarded, since all had remained through a gap in the text before the door of the chief officer's lodging.
And so on the next day, the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the morning a great crowd gathered at Sexti according to the command of Galerius Maximus the proconsul.
And so the same Galerius Maximus the proconsul on that same day ordered Cyprian to be presented to him as he sat in the hall called Sauciolus.
And when he had been presented, Galerius Maximus the proconsul said to Cyprian the bishop, Are you Thascius Cyprian?
Cyprian the bishop answered, I am.
Galerius Maximus the proconsul said, Have you held yourself out as father to men of a sacrilegious mind?
Cyprian the bishop answered, I have.
Galerius Maximus the proconsul said, The most sacred emperors have commanded you to perform the rites.
Cyprian the bishop said, I do not do it.
Galerius Maximus said, Take counsel for yourself.
Cyprian the bishop answered, Do what has been commanded you, for in a matter so just there is no deliberation.

choices.english: the chief officer and the attendant of the same staff
choices.why: princeps here is an official rank in the proconsular officium and strator is a subordinate attendant, so a staff hierarchy fits the custody context
papa in third-century Christian use denotes a bishop as father, and praebere with reflexive sense means presenting oneself in that role to his people
deponent infinitive after commanding verb refers to carrying out the imperial pagan observances, not merely holding ceremonies in general
